# aibris v0.10.0

This release publishes the first versioned machine-readable cleanup plan and
execution receipt contracts under the documented 0.x compatibility policy.

## Highlights

- `aibris clean --dry-run --json` emits a redacted `clean_plan` that separates
  byte-owning physical targets from logical evidence rows. `--include-paths`
  remains an explicit opt-in for paths, projects, and cleanup commands.
- `aibris clean --json --force` and `aibris clean --json --interactive` emit a
  redacted `clean_receipt` for the plan built and executed in the same process.
  Receipts make requested, removed, partial, failed, cancelled, and
  owner-verified freed-byte outcomes machine-readable.
- Windows HOME and cache fixtures are hermetic, and CI exercises the native
  executable with an isolated Windows profile.

## Compatibility impact

**Compatible addition.** v0.10.0 adds `clean_plan` and `clean_receipt` to the
existing machine-readable surface. The schema remains `schema_version: 1`;
existing documented `scan --json` fields, defaults, and exit behavior remain
unchanged. New consumers should follow [the JSON schema](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.10.0/docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md)
and stop on an unknown newer schema version.

JSON execution is deliberately explicit: non-dry-run `clean --json` requires
`--force` or `--interactive` and always uses the classic route. `--guide` is
rejected before scan or mutation for JSON execution. This hardens the
documented route rather than removing a published v0.9.0 JSON execution
contract; dry-run guided JSON planning remains available.

## Upgrade and migration

No migration is required for existing `scan --json` consumers. To automate a
cleanup, first inspect a plan and then run the same classic selectors without
`--dry-run`:

```bash
aibris clean --no-guide --dry-run --json
aibris clean --no-guide --json --force
```

Use `--interactive` instead of `--force` when an automation supplies one silent
confirmation line per selected physical target. A plan or receipt is evidence
only: v0.10.0 has no replay command and never accepts either document as a
future execution input.

For a guided read-only plan, keep `--dry-run`:

```bash
aibris clean --guide --dry-run --json
```

## Safety

- JSON plans fail closed on incomplete scan evidence. Execution repeats plan,
  identity, cached-evidence, Git, and agent-state validation immediately before
  mutation.
- A receipt exits zero only with status `succeeded`. Its `freed_bytes` value is
  credited only when the physical owner is verified absent after a mutation
  attempt; command success alone does not invent reclaimed space.
- Default output is path-redacted. `--include-paths` is the only opt-in that
  includes target paths, projects, or cleanup argv.

## Windows status

Windows archives are **experimental**. The supported shape is the `amd64` /
`arm64` Windows zip archives cross-built by GoReleaser and listed in
`checksums.txt`. Native users verify the SHA-256 and place `aibris.exe` on
`PATH`; `install.sh` remains Unix-only. Pull-request CI builds and exercises
the native executable (`--version`, `--help`, isolated `scan --json`), home /
cache isolation, recorded-cwd volume safety, reparse-point cleanup protection,
and hermetic HOME fixture behavior on `windows-latest`. A Windows version
matrix is not published.

## Verification

Pre-tag verification passed `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and
`go test -race ./cmd` (219.595s). The native Windows binary plus focused `cmd`
tests passed, including PE32+ inspection and Windows cross-compilation. The
curated-release Windows-status validator and diff checks also passed. The
tagged release workflow publishes the six Darwin/Linux/Windows archives and
`checksums.txt`.

The full `go test ./... -count=1` suite also passed under a hermetic HOME with
a 420-second cap (root: 10.066s; `cmd`: 137.844s; all internal packages passed).

### Pre-tag dogfood

A read-only real-home run used `aibris clean --dry-run --json` with its XDG
cache isolated. It exited `0`, emitted one JSON document with empty stderr,
and leaked no home path. The document reported `schema_version: 1`,
`document_type: clean_plan`, `mode: dry_run`, `paths_included: false`, live
complete evidence, and zero provider errors:

| Plan state | Physical targets | Bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| physical | 192 | 37,731,713,257 B |
| selected | 8 | 1,605,922,816 B |
| reviewable | 7 | 496,939,008 B |
| protected | 89 | 2,617,810,944 B |
| skipped | 88 | 33,011,040,489 B |

The real-home run was dry-run only; no deletion occurred.

An isolated-HOME fixture verified the execution boundary. Explicit
`--guide` execution failed before scan with exit `1`, empty stdout, and a
static path-free error. Its dry-run plan was schema version `1` with one
selected `target-1` of 4,096 B and retained the fixture. Classic execution
using `--no-guide --json --force` emitted a schema version `1`
`clean_receipt` with status `succeeded`, exit `0`, `requested: 1`,
`removed: 1`, and `freed_bytes: 4096` for that same `target-1`; stderr and
path leakage were both empty, and only the fixture target was deleted.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.10.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.
